data.title: World can manage without Strait of Hormuz, but no return to pre-war normal - IEA
data.description:
The world can manage without the Strait of Hormuz, but it's unlikely that energy markets can return to where they were before the start of the Iran war, according to the International Energy Agency's head Fatih Birol.

"I don't see any credible pathway back to the situation that existed in Feb. 2026," he wrote in an article for The Economist. "Confidence in the strait as a safe and reliable corridor for energy and other goods has been crushed."

As a result, countries will pay more attention to diversification. "They will pursue a more varied mix of fuels and energy technologies, of suppliers and trade routes," Birol stated. "Those new routes will include pipelines out of the Middle East that bypass Hormuz (the UAE and Saudi Arabia are already moving ahead rapidly on these)."

But while the global energy system can diversify away from the strait over time, he insisted the Middle East will remain vital for energy security and markets.

Birol's statements come as the IEA released The World Energy Outlook 2026 on Thursday, which referred to the Strait of Hormuz disruptions as the world's largest energy supply shock.

"At its peak, global oil supply fell by 16M barrels per day and gas supply by 320 million cubic meters per day," it noted.

Its report found that new bypass pipelines, alternative supplies and measures to displace demand could reduce the need for oil flows through the strait from 20 mb/d before the crisis to 8.5 mb/d in 2030 and to under 2 mb/d by 2035.

"But even in this extreme case, the Middle East would remain the world's largest exporter of oil to international markets," the report affirmed.

Notably, Goldman Sachs expects an additional 3.8 mb/d of pipeline capacity to come online over the next year as Middle East oil producers invest in pipelines that bypass the Strait of Hormuz and transport directly to the Gulf of Oman, Red Sea or Mediterranean Sea.

data.title: Anthropic investors’ shares rise ahead of Claude developer's record market debut
data.description:
Shares of major technology companies invested in Anthropic (ANT) rose in premarket trading on Thursday as the AI startup prepared for its stock market debut.

Amazon (AMZN) shares gained 2.4%, while Alphabet (GOOGL) (GOOG) rose 3.5%. Amazon's stake in Anthropic will amount to 14.7%, while Alphabet will own 13.7%. Both holdings will consist of non-voting shares.

Nvidia (NVDA) climbed 2%, AMD (AMD) added 3%, and Broadcom (AVGO) advanced 2.9%.

Zoom Communications (ZM) was up 2.5%, Microsoft (MSFT) up 1.4%, and Micron (MU) was up 4.2%. But Salesforce (CRM) was down 0.16%.

The iShares AI Innovation and Tech Active ETF (BAI) also rose 4% in premarket trading.

Anthropic priced its shares at $83 apiece, raising $81.3B, which is the largest stock market debut on record. The offering values the company at about $1.5T.

data.title: AM Need to Know: Anthropic prices IPO, Intel lands first 18A-P customer & more
data.description:
U.S. stock futures moved higher early Thursday, with technology shares leading the gains, as investors turned their attention to the highly anticipated public debut of artificial intelligence startup Anthropic.

Now, here are three news stories that broke overnight to watch out for:

Anthropic prices record $81.34 billion IPO above targeted range: Anthropic (ANT)  priced its initial public offering at $83 per share, above its marketed $70 to $78 range, with the offering comprising 980 million shares to raise approximately $81.34 billion. The combined offering surpasses SpaceX's $75 billion debut earlier this year to become the largest IPO on record. Shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday under the ticker symbol ANT, with the offering expected to close on November 20.

Intel secures first external customer for 18A-P foundry process: Intel (INTC) CEO Lip-Bu Tan  announced at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas, that the company has signed its debut outside customer for its 18A-P manufacturing process node, sending INTC shares 2.6% higher in extended trading. Intel's technology chief Pushkar Ranade clarified on X that the customer had signed up for the 18A-P node, which went into risk production in June. The deal marks a milestone in Intel's five-year effort to compete with chip manufacturing leader Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing. Reports in May indicated Apple and Intel were closing in on a deal to use Intel's foundry for some Apple device chips, though Tan did not name the debut client.

Wall Street's $500 billion Nvidia chip financing initiative stalls: A pledge from Wall Street firms to secure $500 billion in  financing for Nvidia (NVDA) chips has failed to materialize, according to the Wall Street Journal. Former CEO Jensen Huang secured commitments from Apollo Global Management, Blackstone, BlackRock, Brookfield Asset Management, Goldman Sachs and KKR in August, with the capital intended for AI customers including OpenAI and Anthropic. No funds have been deployed, the Journal reported, and investor doubt is growing about whether the program will proceed following Huang's exit and the cautious stance of interim CEO Colette Kress, who said on Tuesday's earnings call that the company is "rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments and guarantees."

AbbVie partners with DISCO Pharma in $2.54 billion cancer drug agreement: AbbVie (ABBV) has  agreed to pay up to $2.54 billion to collaborate with Germany-based DISCO Pharmaceuticals on developing novel cancer treatments using next-generation bispecific therapies. DISCO will receive $40 million upfront and up to $2.5 billion in milestone payments to develop AND-gated bispecific therapeutics for solid tumors, along with tiered royalties on worldwide net sales. The approach is designed to recognize cancer cells only when two target proteins are present simultaneously, potentially reducing damage to healthy tissue.

data.title: Evotec, Bristol Myers advance protein pact with 2nd IND nod; EVO shares rise
data.description:
• Evotec SE (EVO) Thursday said that its strategic protein degradation partnership with Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY) has received a second Investigational New Drug acceptance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).
  • The first candidate produced under the partnership entered a Phase 1 clinical trial in advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma in March 2026.
  • The second accepted investigational drug candidate, a cereblon E3 ligase modulator (CELMoD), is expected to enter a Phase 1 clinical trial in 2027.
  • Initiated in 2018, the partnership combines Evotec's high-performance multi-omics screening, AI-supported data analytics, and drug design capabilities with Bristol Myers Squibb's industry-leading CELMoD agent library. 
  • Evotec SE (EVO) shares rose 2.7% premarket.
